open_points.subject: Model M04 — ProjectViewerGrant identity
open_points.text: giving the pair access again creates a new grant record.
open_points.question: Who mints the replacement grant_id, from what inputs, and must it be distinct from every earlier grant_id for the pair?
options: The backend mints a fresh UUID independent of the pair and prior records.
The identifier is supplied by the administrator or caller.
The identifier is derived from the pair plus a generation or other value.
open_points.default_guess: The backend mints a fresh UUID distinct from all earlier records for the pair.

open_points.subject: ProjectViewerGrant revocation action
open_points.text: A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; giving the pair access again creates a new grant record.
open_points.question: When several historical grants exist for a viewer-project pair, does revocation identify an exact grant_id or select the pair's current active grant?
options: Revocation takes grant_id and changes exactly that record.
Revocation takes viewer_id and project_id and changes the unique active record.
Both actions exist with separately stated semantics.
open_points.default_guess: Revocation selects the unique active record by viewer_id and project_id.

witness.initial: Grant G1 for viewer V and project P is revoked, and replacement grant G2 for the same pair is active.
events: An administrator requests revocation while identifying V and P, or while presenting the historical id G1.
outcomes: The exact-id interpretation targets G1 and leaves G2 active.
witness.observer: Viewer V and the administrator reviewing the grant history.

witness.initial: Assignment A1 for staff member S and project P is revoked, and replacement assignment A2 for the same pair is active.
events: An administrator requests revocation while identifying S and P, or while presenting the historical id A1.
outcomes: The exact-id interpretation targets A1 and leaves A2 active.
witness.observer: Staff member S and the administrator reviewing assignment history.

open_points.text: A revoked grant is terminal and no operation reactivates it; granting the pair again creates a new grant record.
open_points.question: When several historical grants exist for a principal-project pair, does revocation identify an exact grant_id or select the pair's current active grant?
options: Revocation takes grant_id and changes exactly that record.
Revocation takes service_principal_id and project_id and changes the unique active record.
Both actions exist with separately stated semantics.
open_points.default_guess: Revocation selects the unique active record by service_principal_id and project_id.

witness.initial: Grant G1 for service principal S and project P is revoked, and replacement grant G2 for the same pair is active.
events: An administrator requests revocation while identifying S and P, or while presenting the historical id G1.
outcomes: The exact-id interpretation targets G1 and leaves G2 active.
witness.observer: The producer attempting its next project-scoped request and the administrator reviewing grant history.

open_points.subject: ProjectViewerGrant history
open_points.text: revoked grants of the pair stay as history.
open_points.question: Which product action, if any, reads or exposes the retained revoked grants?
options: Administrator grant-detail or history actions expose every generation.
Ordinary grant lookup returns active and revoked records.
The records are retained only for internal audit or persistence and no product action reads them.
open_points.default_guess: Administrator-only history or audit reads expose them; authorization reads only the active record.

witness.initial: A viewer-project pair has revoked grant G1 and active replacement G2.
events: An administrator opens the product's grant view for the pair.
outcomes: The view shows both G1 and G2 as history.
The view shows only G2; G1 is retained solely internally.

open_points.default_guess: Administrator-only history or audit reads expose them; authorization reads only the active record.

witness.initial: A principal-project pair has revoked grant G1 and active replacement G2.
events: An administrator opens the product's producer-grant view for the pair.
outcomes: The view shows both G1 and G2 as history.

open_points.subject: ProducerProjectGrant authorization status
open_points.text: Grants are consulted only when the principal's `scope_mode` is `granted_projects`.
open_points.question: When scope_mode is granted_projects, are only active grants authorization-bearing, or are revoked historical grants also consulted as project scope?
options: Only the unique active grant authorizes the project.
Any retained grant for the pair authorizes the project despite revocation.
Revoked grants are read for audit but explicitly excluded from authorization.
open_points.default_guess: Only the unique active grant authorizes the project; revoked grants may be read only as history.

witness.initial: A service principal uses scope_mode granted_projects and its only grant for project P has been revoked.
events: The service principal attempts an import for P.
outcomes: Authorization ignores the revoked grant and refuses project scope.
Authorization finds the retained grant and permits project scope.
witness.observer: The service principal and the administrator who revoked the grant.
